pages.text: "Wow, fruit!" Red fruit lay beneath a tree beside the waterhole. Tumba the warthog poked their snout toward it. Mom said, "That's a snack. You'll eat grass roots for dinner." Tumba was already swallowing eagerly.
"I want lots of sweet things!" While Mom went for a drink, Tumba gobbled fruit. "A little more..." Soon the ground was bare. Kiki stood up, worried. "That much, Tumba?"
At dinner, Tumba's tummy was full and aching. "Too full... I can't eat roots." Their legs shook when they tried to dig. Even with their favorite roots nearby, Tumba lowered their snout sadly.

Mom folded her legs beside Tumba and gently rubbed their tummy with her muzzle. "Your tummy's full." Tumba wrinkled their snout. "But I want roots..." "Next time, I'll show you how to eat just a little."
Mom tapped Tumba's tummy. "It's a little burrow. Fill it with fruit, and there's no room for roots." Tumba imagined roots waiting outside a fruit-filled burrow. "I need to leave room!"
"Always leave some room for roots." Mom drew a small circle in the dirt. "Just a little fruit! Roots first!" Kiki lifted a paw. "Let's promise together!" Tumba peered at the circle.
The next afternoon, more fruit lay under the tree. Tumba ate just a little, then lifted their snout. The rest stayed untouched. It was hard at first, but Tumba did it!
At dinner, Tumba's tummy rumbled softly. They dug and ate roots with delight. "Were roots always this tasty?" Their tummy felt comfortable and their legs strong. Their tail popped up.
Now Tumba knew the rules. "One, just a little fruit! Two, roots first, fruit later! Three, leave the rest!" Next time, Tumba ate a little and turned away from the tree.
Mom touched her muzzle to Tumba's round tummy. "You know when to stop now!" A little fruit and roots first helped Tumba feel comfortable and strong. "Just a little fruit!" Kiki clapped.
